headline: GOLD SLIPS TO $4,508 AS IRAN SUPREME LEADER BANS URANIUM EXPORT; PEACE DEAL IN JEOPARDY
snippet: Spot gold dropped to $4,508 on May 23 after Iran's Supreme Leader issued a directive blocking any export of enriched uranium — killing the central condition the US sought in peace talks. The setback reverses a relief rally that had pushed gold to nearly $4,700 just weeks ago when Strait of Hormuz closure fears eased.

headline: ZIJIN'S C$5.5B ALLIED GOLD TAKEOVER CONFIRMED ON TRACK TO CLOSE MAY 29 — YEAR'S BIGGEST GOLD DEAL
snippet: Allied Gold confirmed this week that regulatory approvals for Zijin Gold's all-cash C$5.5 billion (C$44/share) takeover remain on track ahead of the May 29 outside date. The deal — the largest gold acquisition of 2026 — passed a 97% shareholder vote in March and adds three large open-pit mines in Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, and Ethiopia to Zijin's portfolio.

headline: GR SILVER DRILLS BEST-EVER HOLE: 45.1M AT 1,623 G/T SILVER AT SAN MARCIAL (TSXV: GRSL)
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) reported its best-ever drill hole on May 19 from the SE area of San Marcial, Mexico — hole SMS26-04 returned 45.1 metres at 1,623 g/t silver, including 8.25 metres at 8,579 g/t silver. Three rigs remain active on a 20,000-metre step-out program with a mineral resource update and PEA targeted for H2 2026.

headline: TROILUS DRILLS 2.92 G/T GOLD OUTSIDE RESOURCE NEAR RESERVE PIT — ANALYSTS FLAG M&A POTENTIAL
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) expanded its West Rim discovery on May 19 with a hole returning 2.92 g/t AuEq over 19 metres — entirely outside the current mineral resource and within 200 metres of the North Reserve Pit. The Northern Miner noted analysts are flagging the near-pit grade-thickness intercepts as a potential M&A catalyst; a second phase of drilling is planned for later in 2026.

headline: JUGGERNAUT MOBILIZES FOR INAUGURAL 10,000M DRILL AT DISTRICT-SCALE DISCOVERY, GOLDEN TRIANGLE BC
snippet: Juggernaut Exploration (TSXV: JUGR) mobilized on May 19 for an inaugural 10,000-metre drill program on its Big One property in BC's Golden Triangle. Surface samples from the 22 km² Eldorado zone returned up to 263.70 g/t AuEq, with visible free-milling gold in vein systems up to 10 metres wide; Crescat Capital is a backer and a 5-year drill permit is in hand.

headline: CORE LITHIUM RESTARTS FINNISS MINE AS SPODUMENE REBOUNDS TO $4,200/T
snippet: Australia's Core Lithium restarted blasting and excavation at its Finniss project in the Northern Territory on May 20, as spodumene concentrate prices recovered to approximately $4,200 per tonne. The mine sat on care-and-maintenance since 2024; first ore processing is targeted for Q3 2026 and first shipments for Q4, backed by a A$290 million funding package.

headline: URANIUM SPOT HITS 17-MONTH HIGH AT $86.55/LB AS U.S. BACKS DOMESTIC PRODUCTION PUSH
snippet: Uranium spot prices reached $86.55 per pound — a 17-month high — as the Trump administration fast-tracks domestic production timelines and pledges $80 billion for new reactor construction. Denison Mines' Phoenix ISR project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin has broken ground, the first fully permitted uranium mine to enter construction in over a decade in Canada.

headline: CRITICAL METALS LOCKS IN 15-YEAR RARE EARTH OFFTAKE FOR GREENLAND'S TANBREEZ PROJECT
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. signed a binding 15-year offtake agreement on May 20 covering 15% of Phase 1 production from its Tanbreez project in southern Greenland — one of the world's largest heavy rare earth deposits. REalloys receives priority access to high-value dysprosium and terbium; Critical Metals stock jumped 10% on the news and now has 25% of projected production under binding agreements.

headline: GOLDSEEK ASIAN METALS: GOLD HOLDS ABOVE $4,400 SUPPORT; SILVER DEFENDS KEY $72 FLOOR
snippet: GoldSeek's May 21 Asian metals roundup identifies $4,400 as the critical short-term support floor for gold, with a sustained close below that level needed to break the intermediate bull trend. Silver continues to hold the $72 per ounce zone as structural support; the March 2026 low serves as the technical base for both metals heading into the summer window.

headline: GOLD MINERS FINALLY CATCHING UP TO METAL — ANALYSTS SEE SUSTAINED OUTPERFORMANCE AHEAD
snippet: Multiple analyst desks argue that gold mining equities are entering a sustained outperformance cycle versus physical gold, driven by operational leverage and M&A optionality not reflected in current valuations. Goldman Sachs' $5,400/oz year-end gold target implies significant EPS leverage for producers running $1,200–$1,300/oz AISC — and the valuation gap to bullion has rarely been wider.
